header.Title (Target): Akakashana akanono ka Mulopa-Mulopa mu Mpanga

text.S1: There was once a little girl whose father and mother loved her so dearly they thought nothing too good for her. Her mother made her the prettiest little dresses; Her mother also made for her a little cloak and hood from red cloth, and the little girl looked so pretty in them that her mother called her Little Red Riding-Hood.
text.T1: Patile akantu. Kwali Akakashana ako Ba wishi na Ba nyina batemenwe nganshi, balefwaya ukukaapa fye fyonse efyo kale kabila. Ba nyina bamupangile utumalaya utusuuma nganshi; Ba nyina nakabili Ba mupangile Ba akasote na kakufimba umubili aka mulopa-mulopa, elyo alimoneke bwino icipesha amano efyo Ba mwinike na Akakashana akanono aka Mulopa-mulopa mu Mpanga.
text.T2: Patile akantu. Kwali Akakashana ako Ba wishi na Ba nyina batemenwe nganshi, balefwaya ukukaapa fye fyonse efyo kale kabila. Ba nyina bamupangile utumalaya utusuuma nganshi; Ba nyina kabili ba mupangile akasote na kakufimba umubili aka mulopa-mulopa, elyo alimoneke bwino icipesha amano efyo ba mwinikile na Akakashana akanono aka Mulopa-mulopa mu Mpanga.

text.S1: Little Red Riding-Hood had a grandmother who was so old that sometimes she lay in bed all day and felt too weak to get up.
text.T1: Umukashana alikwete Ba nakulu abakote saana tabakwete na maaka ya kwima mu busanshi. Limo balelalililafye.
text.T2: Umukashana alikwete Banakulu abakote saana tabakwete na maaka ya kwima mu busanshi. Limo balelalililafye.

text.S1: One day the mother called the little girl to her and said, “My child, I have put a pat of butter and some fresh eggs and a cornbread in this basket. Take it and carry it to your grandmother. Run along quickly, and do not loiter nor stop to talk to anyone along the way, for I want you to get back before the afternoon is late.” “Yes, dear mother,” said the little girl, and she took the basket in her hand and set out for her grandmother’s house.
text.T1: Ubushiku bumo, Ba nyina baitile Umukashana na ukumweba ati, "Mwana wandi, nimbika umukate na maani mu museke. Batwalileko banoko-kulu. Wendesheko elyo wilalulumba nokwimanina munshila, ndefwaya ubwele bwangu elyo kacili kasuba." "Emukwai, Ba maayo," efyasosele aka kashana, kabula no museke kalaya ku ng'anda ya banakulu.
text.T2: Ubushiku bumo, banyina baitile Umukashana na ukumweba ati, "Mwana wandi, nimbika umukate na maani mu museke. Batwalileko banoko-kulu. Wendesheko elyo wilalulumba nokwimanina munshila, ndefwaya ubwele bwangu elyo kacili kasuba." "Emukwai, bamaayo," efyasosele aka kashana, kabula no museke kalaya ku ng'anda ya banakulu.

text.S1: Presently she heard feet padding along the path, and the old gray hyena came trotting by. “Good-day, Red Riding-Hood,” said the hyena. “Good-day,” answered the child. “And where are you going this fine bright day with your basket on your arm?” “Oh, I am going to my grandmother’s house. She is so old that sometimes she lies in bed and cannot get up, and I am taking her some butter and some fresh eggs and some cornbread.”
text.T1: Elyo aleenda amfwa amoolu yale mukonka mukashiila, elyo na mumbu uwafitilila aishile alepita. "Mwashibukeni mukwai kakashana," efyasosele chimbwi. "Nga balishani mukwai, akasuba aka", efyasosele Umukashana. " Nikwi uleeya kano kasuba, no museke was fyakulya you?" "Oh, ndeya kuli Ba Mama ku ng'anda. Ba Mama nabakuula limo tabeema na mubusanshi. Eico, ndebatwalilako umukate na maani".
text.T2: Elyo aleenda aumfwa amoolu yale mukonka mukashila, elyo na chimbwi uwafitilila aishile pita. "Mwashibukeni mukwai cikashana," efyasosele chimbwi. "Nga balishani mukwai, akasuba aka", efyasosele Umukashana. " Nikwi uleeya kano kasuba, no museke was fyakulya you?" “Eyoo, ndeya kuli Ba Mama ku ng'anda. Ba Mama nabakula limo tabeema na mubusanshi. Eico, ndebatwalilako umukate na maani".

text.S1: ” And where does your grandmother live?” the hyena asked. “She lives beyond the woods in a little white house with a thatched roof and green blinds, the path runs straight there.” The hyena had now learned all he cared to know. He bade Red Riding-Hood good-by and trotted on briskly. As soon as he came into the woods where Red Riding-Hood could not see him he began to gallop. On and on he galloped as fast as he could, for he was anxious to get to the little white house with the thatched roof and the green blinds before Red Riding-Hood did.
text.T1: " Nikwisa bekala Ba mbuya bobe?" Chimbwi aipwishe. "Bekala kunuma yampanga iyo mu kayanda kaku popa akabuta na umutenge wa fyaani, akakashila eko kaleya mukutulila." Chimbwi yaumfwa fyonse efyo yalefwaaya ukuishiba. Yamushalika naapo, yalaendesha. Lilya afiika mu mpanga umushinga mona Umukashana, alabutukisha, pantu alefwaaya ukufiika ku ng'anda yabanakulu elyo akakashana takalafiika.
text.T2: " Nikwisa bekala Ba nokokulu?" Chimbwi aipwishe. "Bekala kunuma yampanga iyo mu kayanda kaku popa akabuta na umutenge wa fyaani, akakashila eko kaleya mukutulila." Chimbwi yaumfwa fyonse efyo yalefwaaya ukwishiba. Amushalika napo, alaendesha. Lilya afiika mu mpanga umushinga mona Umukashana, alabutukisha, pantu alefwaaya ukufiika ku ng'anda yabanakulu elyo akakashana takalafiika.

text.S1: In the depths of the woods, Little Red Riding-Hood’s grandmother was busy at work. She saw the old hyena go by, and she wondered what he was after. “He’s up to some mischief or other, and that is for sure,” said the grandmother. And she followed on after the hyena to see what he was going to do.
text.T1: Mukati ya mpanga, banakulu Ba kakashana bale bomba. Ba mwene chimbwi ca piita, Ba papa nefyo akonkele. "Uyu chimbwi teendele bwino, pali efyo akonkele" efyasosele Banakulu. Bakonkako nokwailile Chimbwi, balefwaya ukumona efyo alefwaaya ukuciita.
text.T2: Mukati ya mpanga, banakulu Ba kakashana bale bomba. Ba mwene chimbwi ca piita, Ba papa nefyo akonkele. "Uyu chimbwi teendele bwino, pali efyo akonkele" efyasosele Banakulu. Bakonkako nokwailile Chimbwi, balefwaya ukumona efyo alefwaaya ukuciita.

text.S1: On went Mr. hyena, and presently he came to the edge of the forest, and there stood the little white house with the thatched roof and green blinds, and the path led straight up to the door, so the hyena knew that must be where the grandmother lived. He stopped and looked all about him, for he did not want anyone to watch him. He saw no one, however, for the grandmother was still catching up to him. Then the hyena knocked at the door, rat-tat-tat!
text.T1: Chimbwi akonkanyapo no kwenda, elyo afiika na kumpela ya mpanga, elyo bamusanga aleloleshya ng'anda yabo. Elyo chimbwi alishibe ukutiila na londokafye bwino-bwino epali banakulu bantu pa mwinshi. Aloleshya loleshya pantu talefwaya abakumu mona. Tamwenepo umuntu nangu umo. Afikile akonkonshya. Nko-nko-nko!
text.T2: Chimbwi akonkanyapo no kwenda, elyo afiika na kumpela ya mpanga, elyo bamusanga alelolesha ing'anda yabo. Elyo chimbwi alishibe ukutiila na londokafye bwino-bwino epali banakulu bantu pa mwinshi. Alolesha lolesha pantu talefwaya abakumu mona. Tamwenepo umuntu nangu umo. Afikile akonkonshya. Nko-nko-nko!

text.S1: Nobody answered, so he knocked again, rat-tat-tat! Still no one answered, and there was no stir within the house, though the hyena cocked his ear and listened carefully. The hyena pulled the latchstring, the latch flew up, and he pushed the door open, and slipped inside. He looked about, and there was nobody there, for the old grandmother had been feeling stronger that day, so she had dressed and had gone out to pick berries.
text.T1: Takwali aba aswiike, elyo akokwenshye nakabili, nko-nko-nko! Nakabili Takwali aba aswiike, elyo tapali nabalesakanya mu ng'anda Mukati, nangula chimbwi aimya amatwi tapali efyo ale umfwa. Efyo aiswile iciibi naco caisuuka, alengela na Mukati, tamwali umuntu nangu umo rtpantu Ba nakulu bale umfwako amaka balifuumine mu ku swa amalubeni.
text.T2: Takwali aba aswiike, elyo akokwenshe nakabili, nko-nko-nko! Nakabili Takwali aba aswiike, elyo tapali nabalesakanya mu ng'anda Mukati, nangula chimbwi aimya amatwi tapali efyo ale umfwa. Efyo aiswile iciibi naco caisuuka, alengela na Mukati, tamwali umuntu nangu umo pantu Ba nakulu bale umfwako amaka balifuumine mu ku swa amalubeni.

text.S1: The old hyena hunted about until he found the grandmother’s bedgown; then he pulled it on over his big hairy body. He tied on a big ruffled cap and put the grandmother’s spectacles on his nose, and after that he crawled into bed and drew the coverlet up under his chin.
text.T1: Chimbwi umukote yafwailikishe mpaka yasanga ifyakufwaala fyaku sendaminamo; efyo chimbwi afwaala ukufiisa umubili wa mishishi. Abikapo necisote, afwaala na ma gilasi pa mona, efyo aingila na mubusanshi no kuifimbilikisha ukufiisa akanwa akakulu.
text.T2: Chimbwi umukote afwailikishe mpaka asanga ifyakufwaala fyaku sendaminamo; efyo chimbwi afwaala ukufiisa umubili wa mishishi. Abikapo necisote, afwaala na ma gilasi pa mona, efyo aingila na mubusanshi no kuifimbilikisha ukufiisa akanwa akakulu.

text.S1: It was not long before Little Red Riding-Hood came running along, and she was in a great hurry, for she had spent a long-time gathering flower. The grandmother did not see her, however, for she was asleep in the garden. The little girl ran up to the door and knocked upon it, rat-tat-tat! Then the old hyena made his voice very faint and weak like the grandmother’s.
text.T1: Tapakowele, Akakashana nako kafiika, kaishile naka kumpauka pantu kali kokola ukutoola amaluba ya banakulu. Akakashana kabutukiile ku ciibi, no ku konkonshya, nko-nko-nko! Elyo chimbwi abwesha neshiwi ukupalanya kuli banakulu.
text.T2: Tapakokwele, akakashana nako kafiika, kaishile naka kumpauka pantu kali kokola ukutoola amaluba ya banakulu. Akakashana kabutukiile ku ciibi, no ku konkonshya, nko-nko-nko! Elyo chimbwi abwesha neshiwi ukupalanya kuli banakulu.

text.S1: “Who is there?” he asked. “It is I, grandmother; Little Red Riding-Hood,” answered the child. “Pull the latchstring, and lift the latch,” said the hyena. Red Riding-Hood lifted the latch and pushed the door open and went in.
text.T1: "Nibani abo? " baipwishe. "Ninebo, Mama, Akakashana ka mulopa-mulopa aka mu mpanga, efyasosele akaice. " Isuulako we mwana, efyasosele chimbwi. Umukashana efyo aiswile iciibi, aingila na mukati mu ng'anda.
text.T2: "Nibani abo? " baipwishe. "Ninebo, Mama, akakashana ka mulopa-mulopa aka mu mpanga, efyasosele akaice. " Isuulako we mwana, efyasosele chimbwi. Umukashana efyo aiswile iciibi, aingila na mukati mu ng'anda.

text.S1: There was not much light in the room, for the hyena had pulled the curtains across the window. “I am not able to get up, dear child,” said the hyena, still in the same weak voice. “Put your basket on the table and come over here.” Red Riding-Hood did as she was told. She put the basket on the table and came over to the bedside, but as she came closer she thought her grandmother looked very strange.
text.T1: Tamwabutiile saana, pantu chimbwi alibwesha ama katani. " Nsha kwanishe ukwiima," Chimbwi asosele mwishiwi ilya naka." Biika umuseke obe apo wise ku no." Umukashana nao acitile efyo bamwebele nokwisa ku busanshi bwa banakulu, nomba lilya apalama, amona kwati banakulu tabalemoneka bwino.
text.T2: Tamwabutiile saana, pantu chimbwi alibwesha ama katani. " Nsha kwanishe ukwiima," Chimbwi asosele mwishiwi ilya naka." Biika umuseke obe apo wise ku no." Umukashana nao acitile efyo bamwebele nokwisa ku busanshi bwa banakulu, nomba lilya apalama, amona kwati banakulu tabalemoneka bwino.

text.S1: “Oh, grandmother, what big eyes you have,” she said. “The better to see you, my dear,” answered the hyena. “And, grandmother, what long, long ears you have.” “The better to hear you, my dear!” “But, grandmother, what big sharp white teeth you have!”
text.T1: "Yaku, Mama, ameenso ubukulu mwakwata, efyo asosele. " Ekutiila ndekuloleshya bwino, we mwishikulu wandi, efyasosele chimbwi. " Elyo Mama, amatwi ubutaali mwakwata". "Ekutiila ndekumfwa bwino wemwishikulu wandi. Elyo Mama, ameeno ubukuulu mwakwata, elyo ayatwa!
text.T2: "Yaku, mama, ameenso ubukulu mwakwata, efyo asosele. " Ekutiila ndekulolesha bwino, we mwishikulu wandi, efyasosele chimbwi. " Elyo mama, amatwi ubutaali mwakwata". "Ekutiila ndekumfwa bwino wemwishikulu wandi. Elyo mama, ameeno ubukuulu mwakwata, elyo ayatwa!

text.S1: “The better to eat you!” howled the hyena, and he sprang out of bed and caught Red Riding-Hood by the cloak. The little girl cried out, but at this moment the grandmother burst open the door and rushed in. The howl had awakened her from her sleep, and just in time. She struck the hyena with such a blow to the head that it fell down dead.
text.T1: " Ekutiila ninga kuulya bwino!" Efya pundiile chimbwi, elyo afuumine na mubusanshi no ku mwikata Umukashana mwilaya. Umukashana alilila, pali iyi inshita banakulu baishile Ba isuula neciibi. Lintu chimbwi apundile ali Ba busha mutulo. Balichitoba na amaaka yoonse chimbwi ca pona na panshi ninshi nacifwa.
text.T2: " Ekutiila ninga kuulya bwino!" Efya pundiile chimbwi, elyo afuumine na mubusanshi no ku mwikata Umukashana mwilaya. Umukashana alilila, pali iyi inshita banakulu baishile baisuula neciibi. Lintu icipululu calilile ecababushishe mutulo. Balichitoba na amaaka yoonse ichimbwi ca pona na panshi ninshi nacifwa.

text.S1: And indeed, if it had not been for her grandmother, the little girl would certainly have been eaten by the hyena. But from then on Little Red Riding-Hood was careful to obey her mother, and not to loiter on the way when she was sent on errands.
text.T1: Namucishinka, nga te banakulu, Akakashana nga bali kalya kuli chimbwi. Ukufuuma palya, Umukashana ale umfwa ku bafyashi, nokukaana la lulumba nokukaana sosha abantu ebo talingile ukusosha munshila nga na Ba mu tuma ku Ba fyashi bakwe.
text.T2: Namucishinka, nga te banakulu, Akakashana nga bali kalya kuli chimbwi. Ukufuuma palya, Umukashana ale umfwa ku bafyashi, nokukaana la lulumba nokukaana sosha abantu ebo talingile ukusosha munshila nga na Ba mu tuma ku Ba fyashi bakwe.
